column5: A failed profile fetch renders an empty editable form with no error state and saving it submits blank values
column6: The profile page getServerSideProps at src/pages/my-account/profile/index.tsx:937-969 substitutes an empty object for the user on failure - initialData: response.success ? response.data : {} at :956 and initialData: {} in the catch at :965 - and passes no error flag at all. The component reads user = isSSR() ? initialData : userData at :76 and seeds the form from it at :89-96 with name: user?.name || '' and the same pattern for email - mobile - iso_2 - country and friends_code. Every field therefore renders blank with no indication that anything failed. onSubmit at :190-212 then builds new FormData(e.currentTarget) straight from those DOM fields and posts it through updateUserData so a save carries empty strings for the whole profile. Sibling pages already do this correctly - addresses uses response.success ? response.data : null at :284 and surfaces an ErrorState at :131 and the order detail page does the same at :184 - so profile is the only page in the account area that swallows the failure.
column10: SSR mode with the panel returning a failure or timing out on /user/profile - a transient 500 or a dropped upstream connection is enough.
column11: 1. Open /my-account/profile/ while the panel profile endpoint is failing or timing out. 2. Observe the form renders blank with no error message. 3. Press save without editing anything.
column12: The failure is surfaced through ErrorState with a retry exactly as the addresses and order detail pages do - and the form is not rendered as an editable blank.
column13: The form renders as if the account genuinely has no name - no email and no country - and saving posts those empty values back to the panel.
column14: The customer believes their profile has been wiped and can overwrite their real name - email - country and referral code with blanks by pressing save. Whether the write lands depends on panel validation which cannot be verified from this repository - but the blank form with no error state is certain and is a violation of the four required screen states.
column15: Return an error flag from getServerSideProps as the sibling account pages do and render ErrorState with a retry instead of the form. Do not substitute an empty object for a failed fetch - pass null so the difference between no data and failed to load is preserved.

column5: Server side error messages in the account pages are hard-coded English and are rendered directly to the user
column6: Four getServerSideProps handlers put untranslated English into the error prop that the page then renders as the ErrorState description - src/pages/my-account/orders/[slug]/index.tsx:167 Invalid order identifier and :195 Unable to load order details. Please try again later. - src/pages/my-account/orders/index.tsx:409 Unable to load orders. Please try again later. - and src/pages/my-account/addresses/index.tsx:284 Unable to load addresses. Please try again later. Each is passed to description={error} at the matching ErrorState - orders detail :122 and orders list :114 - so the surrounding titles come from t() while the body underneath is fixed English. Translating on the server is awkward because loadTranslations runs per request - which is likely why it was skipped - but the effect is a half translated error panel. This is the same class as issues 16 - 20 and 26 and the count across the app is now 21 files carrying literal user-facing titles.
column10: Application language set to Hindi or Arabic and any server side failure on the orders or addresses pages.
column11: 1. Switch the language to Arabic or Hindi. 2. Force the orders or addresses endpoint to fail so the page renders its error state. 3. Read the panel - the heading is translated and the body is English.
column12: The whole error panel renders in the active language.
column13: The heading renders in the selected language while the description below it stays English - and in Arabic the English body also breaks the right-to-left flow.
column14: Customers in Hindi and Arabic get a partly translated failure message. It also blocks any future copy change because the wording lives in four page files rather than the locale bundles.
column15: Return a stable error CODE from getServerSideProps rather than a sentence and map it to a translation key in the component - which keeps the server handler free of translation concerns and puts the wording in en hi and ar. Then run npm run scan:i18n.

column5: The retry action on four account error states triggers a full page reload rather than refetching
column6: Four account pages wire their ErrorState retry to a hard browser reload - src/pages/my-account/orders/index.tsx:116 - src/pages/my-account/transactions/index.tsx:69 - src/pages/my-account/wallet/index.tsx:107 and src/pages/my-account/refer-and-earn/index.tsx:120 all pass onRetry={() => window.location.reload()}. Every one of these pages already holds an SWR binding that exposes mutate - the orders page destructures the SWR result at :207-208 and the addresses page at :63 - so a scoped refetch is available and is not used. A reload discards the entire SWR cache for the session - re-runs getServerSideProps - re-downloads the bundle - loses scroll position and resets any filter or page held in component state.
column10: Any account page that has rendered its error state.
column11: 1. Open the orders page with the panel failing so the error state renders. 2. Press retry. 3. Observe a full navigation rather than an in-place refetch - the whole app re-initialises and the list returns to its first page.
column12: Retry refetches only the failed request through the SWR mutate the page already has and leaves the rest of the app state intact.
column13: The browser performs a full reload which throws away all cached data and any filter or pagination the user had set.
column14: Slow and heavy recovery from a transient error - the customer loses their place in a filtered order list and pays a full page load for what is one request. On a poor connection this is the worst possible moment to re-download everything.
column15: Pass the SWR mutate the page already destructures as the onRetry handler so only the failed request is retried. Keep the reload only for the offline and maintenance screens where a full re-initialisation is actually the point.
